newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila in new talks with General Motors.
newsitem.headline: Manila in new talks with General Motors.

text.p: The Philippines, beaten by Thailand in a bidding war for General Motors Corp's manufacturing plant in Asia, is holding talks with the U.S. company on building a car component factory in the country, officials said on Sunday. "We've been working on this for eight months," Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista told reporters. He did not give figures, but said capit al expenditures would be "10 to 15 times more than an assembly plant". The project would export to other countries in Asia-Pacific, he said. Bautista said he believed General Motors wanted to set up a components facility as a step towards being accredited to join the Philippines' Motor Vehicle Development Programme (MVDP). Participants in the programme will enjoy such benefits as importation of cheaper stripped car parts for local assembly. One of the requirements of the programme, however, is for a company to set up an assembly plant, Bautista said.
"We cannot change regulations at the drop of a pin," he said.
"What GM wants is to make the Philippines the centre of major car parts and will assemble later on. In their case, it will be the reverse (of the MVDP)," he said.
He stressed, however, that General Motors was not asking for changes to the MDVP, adding, "It is up to us."
Andrew Andersz, public relations director for General Motors' Asian and Pacific operations, last week confirmed the firm had discussed "possible future investments" with Filipino officials.

"While we will not comment on the nature or content of these discussions, we can confirm that the Philippines remains a possible location for future GM investment for component assembly," Andersz said in a statement.
"However, following a recent review, it has been decided that GM will not establish a vehicle assembly operation in the Philippines under the MVDP at the present time," Andersz added.
Bautista said the Board of Investments (BOI) was reviewing the MVDP scheme and hoped to finish the review in August.

"We want to be sure that the programme remains credible and that participants will not be disadvantaged by any change in the regulations," he said. "We want to be sure there is complete transparancy." Thailand last year won the site for General Motors' $750 million-car plant after an intense bidding competition with the Philippines. The Thai plant will build a car targeted exclusively with Asian markets, company officials have said.
